title: Beam Therapeutics Wins FDA IND Clearance for In Vivo Base-Editing PKU Therapy BEAM-304
detail: The FDA cleared Beam Therapeutics' Investigational New Drug application for BEAM-304, an in vivo adenine base-editing therapy delivered by lipid nanoparticle to correct disease-causing PAH mutations that cause phenylketonuria (PKU). BEAM-304 uses a platform-style trial design intended to test multiple mutation-specific base editors for PKU within a single clinical framework, reflecting the FDA's emerging guidance to accelerate genome-editing programs. Beam plans a Phase 1/2 open-label study assessing safety, tolerability, blood phenylalanine reduction, and potential for dietary liberalization in patients with the R408W mutation.

media.caption: Beam Therapeutics announces FDA IND clearance for BEAM-304, an in vivo base-editing therapy for PKU

title: Prime Medicine Wins First-Ever Clinical Clearance for a Prime Editing Therapy
detail: New Zealand's Medicines and Medical Devices Safety Authority cleared Prime Medicine's Clinical Trial Application for PM577a, targeting the ATP7B H1069Q allele responsible for roughly 30–50% of Wilson disease cases in the US and Europe. The clearance is the first-ever human clinical authorization for an in vivo prime editing therapy, enabling a global Phase 1/2 study in adults and adolescents to begin in the second half of 2026, with initial data expected in 2027. Prime Medicine called it a major de-risking event for prime editing as a therapeutic modality distinct from CRISPR-Cas9 and base editing.

media.caption: Prime Medicine announces first-ever clinical clearance for a prime editing therapy, PM577a for Wilson disease
